cards.f: Why use HDI not GNI alone?
cards.b: It combines health, education and income, so it gives a fuller picture.

cards.b: Advantage: jobs and investment. Disadvantage: low wages and profits leave the country.

short.q: Describe the global pattern of development.
short.model: HICs are concentrated in Europe, North America, Japan and Australia, with high HDI. The lowest HDI countries are mostly in sub-Saharan Africa and parts of South Asia, while MICs in Asia and Latin America are developing fast.

short.q: Explain why a high GNI per capita does not always mean a high quality of life.
short.model: GNI per capita is an average, so wealth may be shared unequally. It also ignores health, education and the environment.

short.q: Explain how conflict can hold back development.
short.model: War destroys homes, roads and factories and forces people to flee. Money is spent on weapons rather than schools and hospitals, and investors stay away.

short.q: Explain one advantage of globalisation for a low-income country.
short.model: TNCs set up factories that create jobs and bring investment and technology. Workers' wages raise living standards and taxes pay for services.
points: link to income or living standards

short.q: Explain one disadvantage of TNCs for a host country.
short.model: Wages and safety standards can be poor, and profits are sent to the home country. The TNC may close the factory and move if costs rise.
